one_line: This ad explains how multiple subtle, scientifically-backed facial adjustments accumulate to create a dramatic 'glow-up' effect, promoting Qoves' custom aesthetic reports.

hook.what_happens: Two highly similar female faces are shown side-by-side with the text 'Can you see the differences?'
hook.why_it_works: It immediately engages the viewer's visual curiosity and challenges them to spot subtle details.

shots.description: Side-by-side comparison of the original and subtly edited female face on a solid light-blue background.
Close-up of the edited face with interactive hotspots popping up to label 11 minor adjustments, complete with scientific citations.
Analysis of the original face, highlighting minor flaws (redness, acne, dry hair) in isolated zoom boxes, demonstrating how fixing one does little, but fixing all creates an 'exceptional' look.
An animated line graph comparing the perceived attractiveness over time of 'one big fix' versus 'small changes adding up'.
A rapid scroll of non-surgical techniques leading into a multi-page mockup of a custom 'Qoves' aesthetic report, ending with a search bar CTA.

transcript.text: Take a look at these two faces. Almost everyone would agree that the version on the right is much more attractive.
But can you spot the changes? It wasn't just one thing, or two or three. It was actually eleven tiny adjustments, each supported by the facial aesthetics literature.
And this is a very realistic glow-up. All of the changes we made here can be achieved with scientifically proven, non-surgical methods.
Now, if you met a woman who looked like this, you'd probably say she's pretty and that there's not much she can change. She has no big flaws.
Her eyes just have a tiny bit of redness, she has very mild acne, her hair is just a little dry. It's a bunch of small stuff where fixing one wouldn't change much at all.
But if you fix several small things, that can be the difference between looking like a run-of-the-mill good-looking person, and someone who could star in a film.
This is what people get wrong about glow-ups. They want the big fix, like a nose job or a new hair color, that they imagine will radically transform their look.
But while it might not be as exciting, it's just the truth that usually it's a list of tiny adjustments between you and your best self.

The Qoves database now has over 1000 beautification techniques. So if you want us to write you that list, in the form of a bespoke glow-up plan, and show you a preview of what you would look like at your best self, click the link in bio at Qoves.com.

narrative_arc: Present a visual puzzle comparing two highly similar faces.
Reveal that the preferred face has 11 minor, scientifically-backed edits.
Explain that minor flaws seem negligible individually, but compounding them creates a massive aesthetic leap.
Debunk the myth of the 'one big fix' (like plastic surgery) using a comparative graph.
Introduce Qoves' database of non-surgical techniques and offer a personalized report as the solution.

cta.what: Click the link in bio at Qoves.com to get a custom glow-up plan.

subjects: Unidentified female model (used for the before/after facial comparison).
what_makes_it_work: Uses academic citations to establish high scientific authority.
The interactive hotspot design makes the aesthetic analysis feel objective and clinical rather than subjective.
The line graph clearly conceptualizes the value proposition of 'compounding small changes' over drastic surgeries.

animations.name: Panel Shift
animations.what_moves: Two portrait panels and text callout
animations.purpose: Demonstrates preference by overlapping the preferred face over the other.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing two options where one is highlighted as superior.
animations.would_need_building: A dual-panel layout where one panel slides to partially overlap the other on command.

animations.name: Staggered Feature Callouts
animations.what_moves: Eleven text callout boxes with icons
animations.purpose: Highlights multiple subtle facial edits simultaneously without cluttering.
animations.reusable_as: Showing product features or specifications on an image.

animations.name: Detail Crop Pop-ins
animations.what_moves: Three square image crops with text labels
animations.purpose: Isolates specific facial flaws for closer inspection.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting specific details or defects of a product.

animations.name: Feature Toggle Stack
animations.what_moves: A vertical list of text labels and state badges
animations.purpose: Shows a sequence of improvements toggling from normal to exceptional.
animations.reusable_as: Step-by-step checklist or feature comparison list.
animations.would_need_building: A vertical list component that animates state changes (e.g., text/color swap) sequentially.

animations.name: Graph Path Follower
animations.what_moves: Graph line and a circular face icon
animations.purpose: Visualizes the concept of gradual improvement versus a single big fix.
animations.reusable_as: Showing progress, growth, or journey mapping over time.
animations.would_need_building: An animated line chart where a custom marker/image follows the path as it draws.

animations.name: Report Scroll & Radar Chart
animations.what_moves: Multi-page document and a radar chart outline
animations.purpose: Showcases the comprehensive custom glow-up plan report.
animations.reusable_as: Previewing digital products, PDFs, or multi-page documents.
animations.would_need_building: Integration of an animated radar chart drawing on inside the scrolling container.

animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements scale up with a slight spring bounce or slide in smoothly from the sides.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements fade out or are covered by transitioning panels.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts combined with smooth camera zooms and panel slides.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The background color and main portrait alignments remain consistent.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Highly dynamic, alternating between static explanations and rapid, staggered information reveals.

what_we_should_steal: Staggered Feature Callouts for interactive image detailing.
Graph Path Follower to make abstract data concepts engaging.
Feature Toggle Stack for clean before/after comparisons.
